instruction: I prefer a darker theme for my media player interface. How can I customize VLC's progress slider colors to use a blackish color scheme instead of the default bright colors?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VLC's slider colors to a blackish theme. Uses existing check_qt_slider_colours metric function with type='blackish' to verify all RGB values in qt-slider-colours are below 100 (dark colors). The function parses the semicolon-separated RGB values and validates each color is blackish. No custom functions needed - reuses existing VLC evaluators.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_vlc_config reads the VLC configuration file (vlcrc) from the correct platform-specific location
Metric logic is semantically correct: check_qt_slider_colours with type='blackish' properly parses semicolon-separated RGB values and validates all are below 100 (dark/blackish threshold)
Expected value handling is correct: The rule {'type': 'blackish'} is properly used by the metric to determine which validation logic to apply
Postconfig is appropriate: Killing and relaunching VLC ensures config changes are loaded and readable by the getter
Coverage is complete: The evaluator fully verifies the instruction requirement to use blackish/dark slider colors
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts vlcrc file path -> Metric reads qt-slider-colours setting -> Validates all RGB values < 100
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor concern: The metric function signature check_qt_slider_colours(actual_config_path, rule) differs from standard framework pattern (result, expected, **options). However, this appears to be an intentional custom signature used by multiple VLC metric functions in the codebase, so it should work at runtime.
The threshold value of 100 for 'blackish' is hardcoded in the metric. While reasonable, this could be made configurable if different darkness levels are needed in future tasks.
